source_text: «Ἀμὴν, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ποιῶν ἁμαρτίαν, δοῦλός ἐστι τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ὁ δὲ δοῦλος οὐ μένει ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. Ὁ υἱὸς μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. Ἐὰν οὖν ὁ Υἱὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλευθερώσῃ, ἐλεύθεροι ὄντως ἔσεσθε.» Ἄθρει δὴ οὖν ὅτι τὸ χρῆναι κληρονομεῖν. ἐλευθέροις ἂν πρέποι, καὶ οὐχὶ δὴ μᾶλλον τοῖς ὑπὸ ζυγὰ δουλείας· υἱοὶ γὰρ οἱ μένοντες ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, καὶ οὐχὶ δοῦλοι, φησίν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀστειότατα ἔχει. {ΚΥΡ.} Προσεπάγων δὲ ὁ νόμος τὸ, «Οὐ μὴ λάβῃ ὁ ἀφηγούμενος ἐκ τῆς κληρονομίας τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ, τοῦ κατακληρονομῆσαι τοῖς υἱοῖς
pass_a_gloss: §17 dual gloss: ἐλευθερόω / free · ἐπιούσιος / for-the-coming · διασκορπίζω / be scattered … Pass A scaffolding ≠ Pass B continuous English. Theme: Son frees; ask spiritual goods; prepared lot; one Jerusalem begins.
pass_b_english: Cyril: ‘Amen, amen I say to you that everyone doing sin is a slave of the sin, and the slave does not remain in the house unto the age. The son remains unto the age. If then the Son should free you, you will be free truly.’ (John 8:34–36) So then observe that the needing to inherit would be fitting for free ones, and not rather for those under yokes of slavery; for sons those remaining in the house, and not slaves, he says.
Palladius: It has itself most elegantly.

Cyril: And the law adding the, ‘The leader will not take from the inheritance of his people, to inherit for his sons,’ (Matthew 6:9–13) under-shows some such thing, that Christ would never, for he himself our leader, distribute to some of the sanctified the lot not fitting them. Or is not as it were some other share, and another lot, for those not having altogether dedicated their own life to God; and another and exceptional for those chosen-out and having driven through unto a finishing of the brightness in Christ?

Cyril: So then unbeautiful for saints, the seeking to receive from Christ what is fitting for those in world, and practicing a citizenship the not altogether sanctified. And rather must be sought, nothing fleshly, but all divine and spiritual; thus also the Savior himself was ordering the holy apostles to make the words of the entreaty, shaping the request very well toward the sacred-fitting. ‘For thus,’ he says, ‘you pray: Our Father the in the heavens, let your name be sanctified; let your kingdom come; let your will become, as in heaven also upon the earth. Our bread the for-the-coming give us today, and forgive us our debts, as also we forgive our debtors, and do not bring us into a test, but rescue us from the evil one.’ (James 4:3) So then for those asking not fittingly, what the leader does not give, will be said by us: ‘You ask and do not receive, because you ask badly.’ (Psalm 62:12) And that true is the one saying toward God, that ‘You will give back to each according to his works,’ again the law under-hints for us saying, that ‘For the sake of this cause, the leader will not take, from the inheritance of his people, to inherit his sons, in order that,’ he says, ‘my people may not be scattered each from his inheritance.’ For as it were an own lot has been prepared for each, and analogously to the things set upright the share from God. Or somehow also, he says, it is of the very outlandish for the sanctified to be moved and to desire what those thinking the in world would have, and these temporary and fleshly, and driving past in equal to shadows.
